newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat, await data deluge.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat, await data deluge.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were mostly flat and spreads to Treasuries were unchanged in light trading on Friday, mortgage experts said.
Fixed-coupon pass-throughs traded flat to 3/32 higher overall. No major bid lists were spotted, traders said.
"It's been really quiet today ... spreads are virtually unchanged," said one Ginnie trader at a New York investment firm. Many market participants were on hold for market direction, he said.
Dealers and investors will get fresh market direction from a flood of economic data scheduled for release next week.
Chief among the top-tier data are reports on first-quarter gross domestic product and April employment, slated for release on Wednesday and Friday, respectively.
In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0-percent paper was up 2/32 at 100-14/32, yielding 114 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were up 2/32 as well, at 100-16/32 and 100-23/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were off 1/32 at 6.83 percent, and 10-year notes were off 2/32 at 6.94 percent.
On average, 22 economists forecast the preliminary reading of GDP grew 4.1 percent in first-quarter 1997, up from 3.8 percent in the previous quarter.
Those surveyed said 211,000 new jobs were created in April, up from 175,000 jobs in March. The unemployment rate is expected to hold steady at 5.2 percent.
